title: The Protocol
subtitle: hiring.txt is an open, machine-readable convention for companies to declare their legitimate recruiting practices. This page documents the Tier 0 specification.

overview.title: Overview
overview.p1: hiring.txt is a plain text file published at /.well-known/hiring.txt on a company's canonical domain. It declares which domains, channels, and URLs the company uses for recruiting — and what the company will never ask candidates to do.
overview.p2: Any candidate or tool can fetch the file over HTTPS and compare a recruiter's claims against the company's declaration. No signup, no API key, no intermediary.

format.title: Wire Format
format.p1: The file uses a simple key-value format, one entry per line:
format.rule1: Lines starting with # (after optional leading whitespace) are comments and are discarded by parsers. Inline # does not start a comment — URLs may contain fragments.
format.rule2: Blank lines and whitespace-only lines are silently skipped.
format.rule3: Each data line has the format Key: Value. The first colon is the separator. Keys are case-insensitive.
format.rule4: When the same key appears multiple times, values are unioned (appended, not replaced). This is the primary mechanism for multi-value fields.
format.rule5: Only Canonical-Domains and Never support comma-separated values within a single line. URL-containing fields must use repeated keys because URLs may contain commas.

canonicalDomains.name: Canonical-Domains
canonicalDomains.desc: Domain(s) from which the company legitimately sends recruiting emails.

recruitingChannels.name: Recruiting-Channels
recruitingChannels.desc: Official recruiting channel URLs (LinkedIn company page, careers site). HTTPS required.

applicationUrls.name: Application-URLs
applicationUrls.desc: The only legitimate URLs where candidates may apply. HTTPS required.

never.name: Never
never.desc: Negative assertions — things the company will never do during recruitment. Kebab-case tokens.

verifyContact.name: Verify-Contact
verifyContact.desc: Official contact to confirm a recruiter's legitimacy. Must be mailto: or https:// URI.

reportAbuse.name: Report-Abuse
reportAbuse.desc: Where to report impersonation or fraudulent use of the company's name.

expires.name: Expires
expires.desc: ISO 8601 date-time after which the file is considered stale/unverifiable.

policy.name: Policy
policy.desc: Optional human-readable recruiting policy page. HTTPS required.

verifiedRecruiters.name: Verified-Recruiters
verifiedRecruiters.desc: Optional public profile URLs of authorized recruiters.

lastUpdated.name: Last-Updated
lastUpdated.desc: ISO 8601 timestamp of the last file update. Auto-set by the generator.

neverTokens.title: Well-Known Never Tokens
neverTokens.description: The following tokens are part of the standard registry. Verifiers recognize and match these automatically. Custom kebab-case tokens are allowed but may not be auto-verified.
neverTokens.payment: The company will never ask for payment at any stage.
neverTokens.crypto: The company will never request cryptocurrency transfers.
neverTokens.gift-cards: The company will never request gift card purchases.
neverTokens.personal-email: All communication uses corporate email, never personal.
neverTokens.whatsapp-first-contact: First contact will never be via WhatsApp.
neverTokens.telegram-first-contact: First contact will never be via Telegram.
neverTokens.id-before-offer: Government ID is never required before a formal offer.
neverTokens.bank-details-before-offer: Bank details are never requested before a formal offer.

verdicts.title: Verification Verdicts
verdicts.description: When a candidate uses the verifier, the result falls into one of three categories:
verdicts.verifiedDesc: The recruiter's domain, channel, or profile matches the company's hiring.txt declaration. This is a hard, deterministic match — no guesswork.
verdicts.unknownDesc: The company either has no hiring.txt, or the recruiter's information doesn't match any declared channel. This is the default state — absence of evidence, not evidence of fraud.
verdicts.suspiciousDesc: Heuristic signals indicate potential fraud: lookalike domain, free-mail sender claiming corporate identity, scam language patterns, or violation of a Never commitment.
